Close TaoEngine's Diary 【有时间就来写写枞阳的一些事情】关于康居路 Posted by TaoEngine on 15 July 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . osm的小伙伴们大家好，今天我无意中发现了osm可以写日记然后放在自己的首页中。有的小伙伴分析地区编辑完完整度，有的教大家正确使用地图标签。虽然我注册有三年多了但是论辈分还是个小老弟😂，那我就写写我比较擅长的东西，欸要不我就写写有关家乡的一些事好了哈 关于康居路 枞阳县枞阳镇旗山社区邻近枞阳县人民医院、银塘花苑与银塘星城这三个区域中间有一条三级道路，道路有花坛阻拦，两条单行道形式，双向四车道（高峰期两车道因为两边可以停车） 这条道路的命名其实非常迷，枞阳县地图与天地图将其命名为健康路，而枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件与地名信息系统将其命名为康居路（商业地图通常采用后者）。这条路到底叫康居路还是健康路？ 其实我住的地方离这条路不远，所以经常在傍晚散步时走这条路。根据我的见解以及查阅对应文件的思路，这条路现阶段应该还是命名为康居路为好，至少26年8月之前还是得叫它康居路 1. 根据路灯管理局的路灯标签判断 26年初，县里开展《城市生命线》安全设备部署工作，在大街小巷安装了监测设备，同时县里也提及同日设立路灯管理所。随即4月份县里的每个路灯都贴上了标签，其中这条路的路灯被贴上康居路标签。这项工作是领先于枞阳县地图的制作的，可以认定当前这条道路仍为康居路 2. 根据枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中康居小区存在与否判断 在枞阳县地图中，康居路并未消失而是跑到了旗山小学与中海山水城的区域中间，而它的命名依据是因为附近有个小区名为康居山庄。但是无论是在枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中，还是在旗山社区服务站点地图中，这个不是小区，是银塘村的回迁房，经简单查阅县政府公开文档初步确认区域名为银塘安置地。真正现存的“康居山庄”在妇幼保健院旁边，不过叫康居家园。当然不排除小区未来改名的情况 其次那条路虽然在路灯管理所的标签、附近停车场名称以及路牌中没有给出详细名称，但是在枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中，这条路被命名为安置地路。鉴于规划文件的审图号较枞阳县地图较新，该未分级道路我建议命名为安置地路，而保留原先的康居路命名位置 为啥要写这条路 上次有个过于热心的小伙伴将康居路所在道路标为健康路（与此同时他还把旗山路标为莲城路，而莲城路是天地图的一处过时标记，我有时间在下一次日记里说），希望我的笔记能在我没时间贡献枞阳的时候，给其他人一些有理可循的参考（与此同时我也会夹带一些私货介绍枞阳有什么有意思的地方，比如枞阳中学占据的地方曾经有个自然村叫答咀村，这个村的来历可神奇了，另开一个新坑），望大家多多关照👋 Location: 殷家老屋, 枞阳县, 枞阳镇, 枞阳县, 铜陵市, 安徽省, 246700, 中国 Discussion Comment from TaoEngine on 18 November 2026 at 04:59 打脸了，旗山小学那条路今天立牌子了😭就是康居路，马上改 Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.text: Tarek Atoui: Hold | Tate Modern Performances Exhibition guide Accessibility Discover Tarek Atoui’s exciting new work in Tate Modern’s iconic Turbine Hall Tarek Atoui is a sound artist and composer whose installations change how we experience sound, not only through our ears but through our whole bodies. For the Hyundai Commission, Atoui transforms the Turbine Hall into a vast sonic landscape, bringing ancient families of instruments into dialogue with electronic technologies. Inspired by the unique acoustic and spatial properties of the Turbine Hall, the commission builds on decades of Atoui’s collaboration with instrument-makers, researchers, engineers and musicians. Wind is channelled through a suspended network of bamboo pipes, playing shengs, mouth organs from China and Southeast Asia, in chorus. Korean drums struck by mechanised mallets are dispersed throughout the space alongside Uzbek karnai horns and 3D-printed horns made from sugar resin and bamboo dust. Textiles up to 30 metres long oscillate in response to wind currents of the Turbine Hall. Each material generates and transmits sound in a different way. Microphones embedded within the installation sample the sounds of the instruments and the Turbine Hall itself. Custom software developed by the artist reworks these sounds and plays them back into the space alongside the instruments, so the soundscape is always changing and no two visits are the same. pages.text: Tariffs and Economic Performance | NBER Skip to main content Tariffs and Economic Performance April 1, 2027 — Cambridge, MA Share X LinkedIn Facebook Bluesky Threads Email Link In the decades after the Second World War, the United States was one of the leading proponents of a rules-based international order, and an advocate of multilateral and regional trade liberalization. By 2016, the US average import-weight tariff had fallen to less than 2% by the year 2016. In a stark departure from this historical trend, the United States introduced a sequence of tariffs on trade partners in 2018–2019, with the largest tariffs imposed on China. This turn towards protectionism has continued recently. On April 2, 2025, the United States announced the most sweeping tariff increases since the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of the 1930s. In the wake of these stark changes in the direction of US trade policy, there is pressing need for further economic research on the impact of tariffs on national economic performance. The dominant southpaw capped his pitching Triple Crown season on Wednesday by winning the AL Cy Young Award in a unanimous vote from members of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America. Royals right-hander Seth Lugo was the runner-up, followed by Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase. pages.text: Tarik Skubal wins AL Cy Young Award 2025 Skip to Content DETROIT -- For the first time in a quarter century, an American League pitcher has won back-to-back Cy Young Awards. Tarik Skubal repeated the feat, beating out Boston’s Garrett Crochet and Houston’s Hunter Brown in voting announced on Wednesday . Skubal i s the first repeat AL Cy Young winner since Pedro Martinez in 1999 and 2000. He joins Denny McLain as the only Tigers to win multiple Cy Youngs with Detroit. Like Skubal, McLain won his consecutively, in 1968 and '69. Hall of Famer Hal Newhouser won back-to-back AL MVP Awards in 1944 and '45, a decade before the Cy Young Award was created. All-time Cy Young Award winners “It means a lot,” Skubal said on a conference call with reporters after the announcement. “Anytime you accomplish an award of this presence, honor, it's really cool. And to be the first one in the American League since Pedro [to win back-to-back] is even more special, obviously.” Skubal wasn’t a unanimous winner this year, but he received 26 of 30 first-place votes (198 points) , with the other four going to Crochet (132 points). The two southpaws were first or second on all 30 Baseball Writers' Association of America ballots. Though Skubal didn’t repeat his American League pitching Triple Crown , he was arguably better in some aspects, allowing him to stand out in a strong field of candidates on the AL side. His 6.5 b WAR topped last year (6.4), outpacing fellow finalists Crochet (6.3) and Hunter Brown (6.1). Skubal’s 2.21 ERA was nearly a quarter of a run better than the second-place Brown (2.43).

A common scam geared towards tax pros aims to collect their Electronic Filing Identification Numbers. How the scam works The scammer poses as a tax software provider and emails the tax pro with a request to provide their EFIN information by fax. When the tax pro faxes back their EFIN information, the scammer uses the information to steal client data and file fraudulent tax returns for refunds. Pregnant women can give their babies protection against whooping cough (pertussis) before their little ones are even born. pages.text: Tech Accelerators Program Model - NSF Tech Accelerators | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation Tech Accelerators Program Model Skip to content body NSF Tech Accelerators Transforming research into market-ready technologies U.S. National Science Foundation Tech Accelerators is built on a dynamic and flexible program model designed to support the full lab-to-market life cycle. NSF Tech Accelerators will assess the maturity of a topic and appropriately align investments toward funding teams well-positioned to accelerate deep technology ideas from the lab to market faster than ever before. This flexible approach enables teams to assess the maturity of their research or technology before applying for funding and support. The program model includes three stages: Design, build and scale Design stage The design stage provides an up to 12-month planning effort supported by up to $500,000 in non-dilutive funding per team. Funded teams are guided to create strong multidisciplinary collaborations with deep expertise in a technical topic area, form partnerships and develop their initial ideas into low-fidelity prototypes. Each NSF Tech Accelerator is anticipated to award up to 10 teams per design topic. At the conclusion of the design stage, teams must have a low-fidelity prototype, a strong team and partners and basic marketing products and tools (e.g., product name, branding and logo, pitch deck). pages.text: Ted Turner's case for Hall of Fame on Contemporary Baseball Era ballot Skip to Content ATLANTA – When evaluating the impact Ted Turner had on baseball and the entire sports world, you can look at the incredible power sports television has gained in the five decades that have passed since Turner had this crazy idea to use his new satellite network to beam Braves games into living rooms across the world. "Ted Turner was a visionary whose impact on the media landscape transformed how fans experience sports,” MLB Commissioner Robert Manfred said in a statement issued when the former Braves owner passed away in May . Turner is one of eight individuals on this year’s Contemporary Baseball Era ballot , which is reserved for managers, executives and umpires who made significant contributions to the game dating back to the late 20th century. This year’s ballot also includes Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, Sandy Alderson, Joe Maddon, Lou Piniella, Brian Sabean and Bill White. A 16-member panel consisting of Hall of Fame players, Major League executives, media members and historians will consider each of the eight candidates, who must receive at least 75% of the vote to be elected. The results of the Class of 2027 ballot will be announced on Dec. 6. One of the world’s great media moguls, Turner founded WTBS, which is now known worldwide as TBS, and CNN, the first 24-hour cable news channel. Keep in mind that you’re teaching about money, on purpose or not Your children are constantly watching and listening, so they might absorb more than you think. Play to your strengths Even if you don’t think of yourself as a money expert, you do have skills that you already use to navigate your financial life. Things you do naturally may be strengths you can share with your kids. pages.text: Teesside conservationists search for European eels in River Tees Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Conservationists searching for large river eels 8 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Tom Burgess North East and Cumbria Tees Rivers Trust Tees Rivers Trust workers have been tagging eels to track their downstream migration Conservationists have spent summer and autumn searching for critically endangered eels to tag as they begin their downstream migration. The Tees Rivers Trust have found 12 large eels by fyke netting, a method of catching eels with a cylindrical net, around the River Tees catchment. The team managed to electronically tag 10 of them and the largest was 60cm (23ins) in length and weighted 435g (0.9lbs). Project manager Ellie Ward said the eels caught this year were not as large as usual and were "harder to catch". The team has been searching for "silver" eels which have finished maturing and are preparing to head back out to the Sargasso Sea near Bermuda. Ward said: "European eels start to migrate downstream during autumn and winter, when river discharges increase. "We suspect that low flows in summer that have continued into autumn have contributed to low catch rates so far this year." pages.description: Nikkolas Smith, the bestselling illustrator, has a new children's book that takes a look at the innovative, creative dawn of our species.
pages.text: Telling the story of humanity’s origins in Africa—this time, for kids | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Telling the story of humanity’s origins in Africa—this time, for kids Nikkolas Smith, the bestselling illustrator, has a new children's book that takes a look at the innovative, creative dawn of our species. The illustrator Nikkolas Smith, surrounded by his original canvas paintings for his new children's book, The History of We. Photograph By Vanessa Crocini By Kyndall Cunningham Published June 11, 2025 You’ve probably heard that we can all trace our roots back to Africa. It’s a fact that most people learn about briefly in a history class or find out through 23andMe. Still, this shared origin story often feels like a blip in our consciousness compared to other time periods. It’s a commonality we’re willing to acknowledge but not always explore. Picture-book author and film illustrator Nikkolas Smith fills in this curiosity gap with his latest book, The History of We , which he both wrote and illustrated. The self-described “artivist” has dedicated much of his career to rendering crucial moments and people in Black history through expressive paintings, from portraits of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor to a comic-book treatment of the Obamas. One of his most well-known projects is The 1619 Project: Born on the Water, the children’s adaptation of the New York Times venture led by Nikole-Hannah Jones, which he illustrated. With The History of We , Smith continues this tradition of documenting Black history in a way that’s accessible, honest, and completely mesmerizing.

Get our Newsletter! Like many birds, domestic turkeys, including this group at the Smithsonian's National Zoo in Washington, D.C., are social animals. Smithsonian/Brett Kuxhausen 1. Humans have been raising turkeys for thousands of years. Although indigenous peoples in North America have hunted wild turkeys since the end of the last Ice Age, the animals were first domesticated in Mexico around 2,000 years ago. Dinner wasn’t the original goal: archaeological evidence suggests turkeys were initially kept so their feathers could be used in clothing and ceremonial regalia. By A.D. 500, people were raising turkeys in what is now the United States too, judging by archaeological remains from caves in Arizona and New Mexico. Even so, those weren’t the birds that English settlers ate in the Thirteen Colonies. The domestic turkey descends from a southern Mexican bird that the Spanish took home in the 1500s. The birds then spread through Europe, and colonists brought them back across the Atlantic. The bird’s English name may reflect this long-distance trade: turkeys are thought to have reached England along winding trading routes that first passed through the country of Turkey. 2. pages.title: Tennis: Britain's Henry Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for trophy presentation absence - BBC Sport
pages.description: Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticises the ATP's chairman and CEO for missing the year-end world number one trophy presentation.
pages.text: Tennis: Britain's Henry Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for trophy presentation absence - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Henry Patten (left) and Harri Heliovaara have won five titles in 2026, including Wimbledon By Harry Poole BBC Sport journalist Published 17 November 2026 Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticised the ATP's chairman and CEO for their absence at Monday's year-end world number one trophy presentation. Wimbledon champions Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara received their trophy ​from the ATP's chief tour officer Andre Silva in Turin, after ending the season as the top-ranked men's doubles pairing for the first time. In his acceptance speech, Patten, 30, called out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO ​Eno Polo for their decision not to attend. "What a journey it has been. Turin is such a special place for us, we played a challenger just across the road when we ranked 60 and 40 in the world a couple of years ago. I never would ​have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now," said Patten. "For ​us it's a really big deal. ​It's a real shame that the ATP ‌chairman ⁠and the ATP CEO don't think the same. "It would have been nice to have them on ​court with ​us ⁠today, but here we are by ourselves. "We have worked incredibly hard and thank you all for appreciating that." pages.description: Heavy rain has flooded temporary shelters used by Palestinians displaced during Israel's war with Hamas.
pages.text: Tens of thousands of tents flooded after heavy rains in Gaza Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Tens of thousands of tents flooded after heavy rains in Gaza 7 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Emer Moreau Getty Images Ninety percent of Gaza residents have been displaced by the Israeli war against Hamas Heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents where displaced residents have been living in Gaza, with a United Nations official saying almost everyone in the territory needs help. Residents used pots and pans to clear water from their flooded tents, with some saying they were left without shelter. Jonathan Veitch, the Unicef representative for Palestine, said the "desperate" situation was being made worse by Israeli restrictions on the entry of heavy machinery and supplies such as engine oil. Some 90% of Gaza residents have been displaced by the Israeli war against Hamas, many of them multiple times, with limited access to clean water and sanitation. Aid agencies say the situation is likely to worsen with the start of the rainy season. Speaking to the BBC from Deir Al Balah in central Gaza, Veitch said: "It's just horrific and they're absolutely desperate. "We're providing all the assistance that we can but we're getting stopped on the street as we're driving now because people are begging us for help."
